entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 9 Ho 9:1-17 . <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12354"/><div sID="gen22583" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12354"/><hi type="bold">3. return to Egypt--</hi>(See on <reference osisRef="Hos.8.13">Ho 8:13</reference>). As in <reference osisRef="Hos.11.5">Ho 11:5</reference> it is said, "He shall not return into ... Egypt." Fairbairn thinks it is not the exact country that is meant, but the bondage state with which, from past experience, Egypt was identified in their minds. Assyria was to be a second Egypt to them. <reference osisRef="Deut.28.68">De 28:68</reference>, though threatening a return to Egypt, speaks (<reference osisRef="Deut.28.36">De 28:36</reference>) of their being brought to a nation which neither they nor their fathers had known, showing that it is not the literal Egypt, but a second Egypt-like bondage that is threatened.<div eID="gen22583" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22584" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">eat unclean things in Assyria--</hi>reduced by necessity to eat meats pronounced unclean by the Mosaic law (<reference osisRef="Ezek.4.13">Eze 4:13</reference>). See <reference osisRef="2Kgs.17.6">2Ki 17:6</reference>. <div eID="gen22584" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12358"/><div sID="gen22595" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12358"/><hi type="bold">7. visitation--</hi>vengeance: punishment (<reference osisRef="Isa.10.3">Is 10:3</reference>).<div eID="gen22595" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22596" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Israel shall know it--</hi>to her cost experimentally (<reference osisRef="Isa.9.9">Is 9:9</reference>).<div eID="gen22596" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22597" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the prophet is a fool--</hi>The false prophet who foretold prosperity to the nation shall be convicted of folly by the event.<div eID="gen22597" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22598" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the spiritual man--</hi>the man pretending to inspiration (<reference osisRef="Lam.2.14">La 2:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.13.3">Eze 13:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.3.11">Mi 3:11</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.4">Zep 3:4</reference>).<div eID="gen22598" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22599" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">for the multitude of thine iniquity, &c.--</hi>Connect these words with, "the days of visitation ... are come"; "the prophet ... is mad," being parenthetical.<div eID="gen22599" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22600" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the great hatred--</hi>or, "the great provocation" [Henderson]; or, "(thy) great apostasy" [Maurer]. English Version means Israel's "hatred" of God's prophets and the law. <div eID="gen22600" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 7. visitation-- vengeance: punishment ( Is 10:3 ). Israel shall know it-- to her cost experimentally ( Is 9:9 ). the prophet is a fool-- The false prophet who foretold prosperity to the nation shall be convicted of folly by the event. the spiritual man-- the man pretending to inspiration ( La 2:14 ; Eze 13:3 ; Mi 3:11 ; Zep 3:4 ). for the multitude of thine iniquity, &c.-- Connect these words with, "the days of visitation ... are come"; "the prophet ... is mad," being parenthetical. the great hatred-- or, "the great provocation" [Henderson]; or, "(thy) great apostasy" [Maurer]. English Version means Israel's "hatred" of God's prophets and the law.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12359"/><div sID="gen22601" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12359"/><hi type="bold">8. The watchman ... was with my God--</hi>The spiritual watchmen, the true prophets, formerly consulted my God (<reference osisRef="Jer.31.6">Jr 31:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hab.2.1">Ha 2:1</reference>); but their so-called prophet is a snare, entrapping Israel into idolatry.<div eID="gen22601" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22602" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">hatred--</hi>rather, "(a cause of) apostasy" (see <reference osisRef="Hos.9.7">Ho 9:7</reference>) [Maurer].<div eID="gen22602" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22603" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">house of his God--</hi>that is, the state of Ephraim, as in <reference osisRef="Hos.8.1">Ho 8:1</reference> [Maurer]. Or, "the house of his (false) god," the calves [Calvin]. Jehovah, "my God," seems contrasted with "his God." Calvin's view is therefore preferable. <div eID="gen22603" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12361"/><div sID="gen22605" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12361"/>10. As the traveller in a wilderness is delighted at finding grapes to quench his thirst, or the early fig (esteemed a great delicacy in the East, <reference osisRef="Isa.28.4">Is 28:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.24.2">Jr 24:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.7.1">Mi 7:1</reference>); so it was My delight to choose your fathers as My peculiar people in Egypt (<reference osisRef="Hos.2.15">Ho 2:15</reference>).<div eID="gen22605" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22606" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">at her first time--</hi>when the first-fruits of the tree become ripe.<div eID="gen22606" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22607" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">went to Baal-peor--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Num.25.3">Nu 25:3</reference>): the Moabite idol, in whose worship young women prostituted themselves; the very sin Israel latterly was guilty of.<div eID="gen22607" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22608" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">separated themselves--</hi>consecrated themselves.<div eID="gen22608" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22609" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">unto that shame--</hi>to that shameful or foul idol (<reference osisRef="Jer.11.13">Jr 11:13</reference>).<div eID="gen22609" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22610" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">their abominations were according as they loved--</hi>rather, as Vulgate, "they became abominable like the object of their love" (<reference osisRef="Deut.7.26">De 7:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.115.8">Psa 115:8</reference>). English Version gives good sense, "their abominable idols they followed after, according as their lusts prompted them" (<reference osisRef="Amos.4.5">Am 4:5</reference>, Margin). <div eID="gen22610" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 10. As the traveller in a wilderness is delighted at finding grapes to quench his thirst, or the early fig (esteemed a great delicacy in the East, Is 28:4 ; Jr 24:2 ; Mi 7:1 ); so it was My delight to choose your fathers as My peculiar people in Egypt ( Ho 2:15 ). at her first time-- when the first-fruits of the tree become ripe. went to Baal-peor-- ( Nu 25:3 ): the Moabite idol, in whose worship young women prostituted themselves; the very sin Israel latterly was guilty of. separated themselves-- consecrated themselves. unto that shame-- to that shameful or foul idol ( Jr 11:13 ). their abominations were according as they loved-- rather, as Vulgate, "they became abominable like the object of their love" ( De 7:26 ; Psa 115:8 ). English Version gives good sense, "their abominable idols they followed after, according as their lusts prompted them" ( Am 4:5 , Margin).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12363"/><div sID="gen22613" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12363"/>12. Even though they should rear their children, yet will I bereave them (the Ephraimites) of them (<reference osisRef="Job.27.14">Job 27:14</reference>).<div eID="gen22613" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen22614" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">woe ... to them when I depart--</hi>Yet the ungodly in their madness desire God to depart from them (<reference osisRef="Job.21.14">Job 21:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.22.17">22:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.8.34">Mt 8:34</reference>). Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus ... in a pleasant place-- that is, in looking towards Tyrus (on whose borders Ephraim lay) I saw Ephraim beautiful in situation like her (Eze 26:1-28:26). is planted-- as a fruitful tree; image suggested by the meaning of "Ephraim" ( Ho 9:11 ). bring forth his children to the murderer-- ( Ho 9:16 ; Ho 13:16 ). With all his fruitfulness, his children shall only be brought up to be slain.
